A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset agitation,
hallucinations, disorganized thinking, and frequent orofacial dyskinesias. According to her roommate,
she initially experienced memory loss and has now progressed to an almost unresponsive state. Two
days prior to these symptoms, she had a low-grade fever and headache. Her medical history is
unremarkable, and she has no recent sick contacts or history of illicit drug use. She occasionally drinks
wine but takes no daily medications. On examination, her temperature is 102.9 ºF, blood pressure is
171/107 mmHg, pulse is 51/min, and respiratory rate is 11/min. She has a reduced level of
consciousness and frequent orofacial dyskinesias. A head CT scan is normal. Lumbar puncture with
cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows lymphocyte pleocytosis and elevated IgG antibodies targeting
anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors. Which underlying condition is most commonly linked to this
clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Hodgkin lymphoma (B) Small cell lung cancer (C) Testicular
germ cell tumor (D) Ovarian teratoma (E) Viral encephalitis (F) Neuroblastoma (G) Glioblastoma
multiforme (H) Hashimoto's encephalopathy (I) Systemic lupus erythematosus (J) Thymoma
 A. Glioblastoma multiforme
B. Systemic lupus erythematosus
C. Hodgkin lymphoma
D. Small cell lung cancer
E. Testicular germ cell tumor
F. Neuroblastoma
G. Ovarian teratoma
H. Thymoma
I. Viral encephalitis
J. Hashimoto's encephalopathy
